coordinateNote: Pins mark a representative point on the crossing or a tunnel portal, not a country or state center.

cards.name: Brooklyn Bridge
cards.fact: The Brooklyn Bridge crosses New York’s East River with stone towers, suspension cables, and extra diagonal stays.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge and approaches: 6,016 ft.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1883; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.originalFilename: Brooklyn Bridge and the Lower Manhattan skyline from Pebble Beach, New York.jpg

cards.name: Manhattan Bridge
cards.fact: The Manhattan Bridge carries road, subway, bike, and foot traffic between Lower Manhattan and Brooklyn.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: 6,855 ft.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1909; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Williamsburg Bridge
cards.fact: The Williamsburg Bridge links Manhattan's Lower East Side with Brooklyn and was once the world's longest suspension span.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: 7,308 ft.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1903; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Queensboro Bridge
cards.fact: The Queensboro Bridge crosses the East River by Roosevelt Island and is also known as the Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge and approaches: 7,449 ft; the 3,725 ft figure excludes approaches.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1909; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge

location.label: Brooklyn–Staten Island, New York, United States

cards.fact: The Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge connects Brooklyn and Staten Island with a giant suspension span over the Narrows.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: 13,700 ft; the main span alone is 4,260 ft.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1964; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: George Washington Bridge

location.label: Manhattan, New York–Fort Lee, New Jersey, United States

cards.fact: The George Washington Bridge crosses the Hudson River and is one of the world's busiest motor-vehicle bridges.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: 4,760 ft; the main span alone is 3,500 ft.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1931; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.originalFilename: George Washington Bridge from New Jersey-edit.jpg

cards.name: Robert F. Kennedy Bridge
cards.fact: The Robert F. Kennedy Bridge, often called the Triborough, ties Manhattan, Queens, and the Bronx together.
cards.lengthNote: Combined branches: 17,710 ft, excluding elevated ramps. This complex has three branches, rather than one end-to-end route.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1936; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Bronx-Whitestone Bridge
cards.fact: The Bronx-Whitestone Bridge gives drivers a direct East River route between the Bronx and Queens.
cards.lengthNote: Suspension structure: 3,770 ft, excluding approach roads.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1939; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.originalFilename: Whitestone Bridge from Clason Point Park.jpg

cards.name: Throgs Neck Bridge
cards.fact: The Throgs Neck Bridge is a major suspension bridge connecting the Bronx and Queens near Long Island Sound.
cards.lengthNote: Total crossing: 11,250 ft including approaches; 2,910 ft is only the length between anchorages.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1961; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Henry Hudson Bridge
cards.fact: The Henry Hudson Bridge is a tall steel arch crossing the Harlem River Ship Canal in northern Manhattan.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: 2,208 ft; the arch span alone is 841 ft.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1936; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Bayonne Bridge

location.label: Staten Island, New York–Bayonne, New Jersey, United States

cards.fact: The Bayonne Bridge's roadway was raised so larger ships could pass beneath its graceful steel arch.
cards.lengthNote: Current bridge and approach viaducts: 7,160 ft, per the Port Authority brochure.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1931; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Goethals Bridge

location.label: Staten Island, New York–Elizabeth, New Jersey, United States

cards.fact: The modern Goethals Bridge uses cable-stayed towers to connect Staten Island with Elizabeth, New Jersey.
cards.lengthNote: Modern bridge length: 7,109 ft; one span, not the sum of the parallel roadways.
cards.openedNote: First modern span opened in 2017; the second opened in 2018. The original 1928 bridge was replaced.
cards.originalFilename: New Goethals Bridge from airplane cropped.jpg

cards.name: Governor Mario M. Cuomo Bridge

location.label: Tarrytown–South Nyack, New York, United States

cards.fact: The Governor Mario M. Cuomo Bridge replaced the old Tappan Zee Bridge across one of the Hudson River's widest points.
cards.lengthNote: The Thruway Authority describes the current bridge as 3 miles long; the walking path is longer.
cards.openedNote: First span opened in 2017; the second opened in 2018. The original Tappan Zee Bridge opened in 1955.

cards.name: Golden Gate Bridge

location.label: San Francisco–Marin County, California, United States

cards.fact: The Golden Gate Bridge's orange towers and foggy bay setting make it one of the most recognizable bridges on Earth.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge and approaches: 8,980 ft; the main suspension span is 4,200 ft.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1937; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.originalFilename: Golden Gate Bridge as seen from Battery East.jpg

cards.name: Tower Bridge
cards.fact: Tower Bridge combines two castle-like towers with a roadway that can lift for tall ships on the Thames.
cards.lengthNote: Approx. 244 m for the bridge, excluding approach roads; measurements including abutments differ.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1894; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: London Bridge
cards.fact: London Bridge is famous because bridges at this crossing have linked the City of London and Southwark for centuries.
cards.lengthNote: Current concrete bridge: 269 m; this is the bridge in London, not the relocated bridge in Arizona.
cards.openedNote: Current concrete bridge opened in 1973; earlier London Bridges stood at this crossing.
cards.originalFilename: London Bridge from St Olaf Stairs.jpg

cards.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
cards.fact: Sydney Harbour Bridge is nicknamed the Coathanger because of its huge steel arch over the harbor.
cards.lengthNote: Total length including approaches: 1,149 m; the arch span is 503 m.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1932; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Akashi Kaikyo Bridge
cards.fact: The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge has one of the longest central spans ever built for a suspension bridge.
cards.lengthNote: Total length: 3,911 m; the central suspension span is 1,991 m.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1998; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Millau Viaduct
cards.fact: The Millau Viaduct soars above France's Tarn valley and is famous for its very tall, elegant piers.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: 2,460 m.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2004; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Ponte Vecchio
cards.fact: Ponte Vecchio is a medieval Florence bridge lined with shops, making it feel like a tiny street over water.
cards.lengthNote: Approx. 95 m for the whole bridge; the central arch spans about 30 m.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1345; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.originalFilename: Ponte Vecchio from Ponte alle Grazie.jpg

cards.name: Rialto Bridge
cards.fact: The Rialto Bridge is Venice's famous stone crossing over the Grand Canal.
cards.lengthNote: Whole bridge: 48 m; the central arch spans about 32 m.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1591; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Charles Bridge
cards.fact: Charles Bridge is a stone bridge lined with statues and is one of Prague's best-known landmarks.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: 515.8 m.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1402; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.originalFilename: Prague 07-2016 view from Lesser Town Tower of Charles Bridge img3.jpg

cards.name: Forth Bridge
cards.fact: The Forth Bridge is a bold red railway cantilever bridge and a UNESCO-listed engineering landmark.
cards.lengthNote: Railway bridge length: 8,094 ft; this is distinct from the neighboring road bridges.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1890; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Oresund Bridge
cards.fact: The Oresund Bridge links Denmark and Sweden, then continues through a tunnel on the same crossing.
cards.lengthNote: Bridge section only: 7,845 m. The artificial island and Drogden Tunnel are excluded.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2000; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.originalFilename: Øresund Bridge from the air in September 2015.jpg

cards.name: 15 July Martyrs Bridge
cards.fact: The 15 July Martyrs Bridge, often called the Bosphorus Bridge, links Europe and Asia across Istanbul's strait.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: 1,560 m; the central span is 1,074 m.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1973; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge
cards.fact: The Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge carries high-speed rail and is widely listed as the longest bridge in the world.
cards.lengthNote: Full railway viaduct: 164.8 km; not one unsupported span.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2011; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge
cards.fact: The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau crossing mixes long sea bridges, artificial islands, and an undersea tunnel.
cards.lengthNote: Full 55 km crossing system including link roads; the central bridge-tunnel section is shorter.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2018; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.originalFilename: West section of Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge (20180902174105).jpg

cards.name: Mackinac Bridge

location.label: Straits of Mackinac, Michigan, United States

cards.fact: The Mackinac Bridge stretches between Michigan's peninsulas and is one of North America's great suspension bridges.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge and approaches: 26,372 ft; commonly rounded to 5 miles.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1957; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Sunshine Skyway Bridge
cards.fact: The Sunshine Skyway Bridge is known for bright yellow cables rising over Tampa Bay.
cards.lengthNote: Full modern crossing: 4.14 miles; the cable-stayed main span is 1,200 ft.
cards.openedNote: Current cable-stayed crossing opened in 1987, replacing earlier bridges.

cards.name: Bixby Creek Bridge
cards.fact: Bixby Creek Bridge is a beloved concrete arch on California's Pacific Coast Highway.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: 714 ft; the central arch spans 360 ft.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1932; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.originalFilename: Bixby Creek Bridge, California, USA - May 2013.jpg

cards.name: Gotthard Base Tunnel
cards.fact: The Gotthard Base Tunnel runs under the Alps and is one of the longest railway tunnels in the world.
cards.lengthNote: One main rail bore: 57.09 km; parallel bores and service passages are not added together.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2016; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Seikan Tunnel
cards.fact: The Seikan Tunnel carries trains between Honshu and Hokkaido with a long section under the seabed.
cards.lengthNote: Full rail tunnel: 53.85 km, including land sections; only 23.3 km lies beneath the seabed.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1988; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Channel Tunnel
cards.fact: The Channel Tunnel, or Chunnel, lets trains travel beneath the English Channel between Britain and France.
cards.lengthNote: Full tunnel route: 50.46 km; parallel rail bores and the service tunnel are not added together.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1994; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.imageCredit: Billy69150 (voir les conditions d'utilisation / see licensing below) · CC BY-SA 4.0
cards.originalFilename: TGV TMST 3011-2 - Sortie Tunnel sous la Manche à Coquelles.jpg

cards.name: Loetschberg Base Tunnel
cards.fact: The Loetschberg Base Tunnel is a long Swiss railway tunnel that slices through the Alps.
cards.lengthNote: Main rail tunnel: about 34.58 km.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2007; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Guadarrama Tunnel
cards.fact: The Guadarrama Tunnel carries high-speed trains through the mountains north of Madrid.
cards.lengthNote: One rail bore: about 28.4 km; the two bores are not added together.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2007; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel

location.label: Virginia Beach–Eastern Shore, Virginia, United States

cards.fact: The Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel uses bridges, trestles, islands, and tunnels to cross the mouth of Chesapeake Bay.
cards.lengthNote: Shore-to-shore crossing: 17.6 miles, including bridges, tunnels and islands; land approach roads are excluded.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1964; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.originalFilename: 2017-07-12 11 23 10 View south along U.S. Route 13 (Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel) crossing the North Channel of the Chesapeake Bay in Northampton County, Virginia.jpg

cards.name: Laerdal Tunnel
cards.fact: The Laerdal Tunnel is a very long road tunnel in Norway with special caverns that break up the drive.
cards.lengthNote: Full road tunnel: 24.51 km.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2000; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Yamate Tunnel
cards.fact: The Yamate Tunnel is a long urban road tunnel carrying expressway traffic under Tokyo.
cards.lengthNote: Completed road tunnel route: 18.2 km; not the combined length of its two bores.
cards.openedNote: First section opened in 2007; the full 18.2 km route was completed in 2015.
cards.imageCredit: 妖精書士 at ja.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0

cards.name: Zhongnanshan Tunnel
cards.fact: The Zhongnanshan Tunnel is a major road tunnel through China's Qinling mountains.
cards.lengthNote: One road bore: 18.04 km; the two parallel bores are not added together.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2007; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.originalFilename: 柞水 秦岭终南山公路隧道南口.jpg

cards.name: Gotthard Road Tunnel
cards.fact: The Gotthard Road Tunnel gives highway traffic a long route through the Swiss Alps.
cards.lengthNote: Original road tunnel: 16.942 km; excludes the separate railway tunnels.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1980; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Tokyo Bay Aqua-Line
cards.fact: The Tokyo Bay Aqua-Line combines a bridge, an artificial island, and a tunnel under Tokyo Bay.
cards.lengthNote: Whole bridge-tunnel route: about 15 km, including both bridge and tunnel sections.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1997; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Ryfylke Tunnel
cards.fact: The Ryfylke Tunnel dives under a Norwegian fjord and is one of the world's longest undersea road tunnels.
cards.lengthNote: Full road tunnel: 14.4 km; one route, not both parallel bores added together.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2019; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Monitor–Merrimac Memorial Bridge–Tunnel
cards.fact: The Monitor–Merrimac carries I-664 over and under Hampton Roads. Its tunnel lets large ships pass above the road.
cards.lengthNote: Whole bridge-tunnel crossing: 4.6 miles; not just the submerged tunnel.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1992; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.imageCredit: Scrap104 at English Wikipedia · Public domain

cards.name: Hampton Roads Bridge–Tunnel
cards.fact: The Hampton Roads Bridge–Tunnel carries I-64 between Hampton and Norfolk, switching from bridges to a tunnel beneath the busy harbor.
cards.lengthNote: Whole bridge-tunnel crossing: about 3.5 miles; not just the submerged tunnel.
cards.openedNote: First tunnel opened in 1957; the parallel tunnel opened in 1976. Length describes the established crossing, not the expansion project corridor.

cards.name: James River Bridge

location.label: Newport News–Isle of Wight County, Virginia, United States

cards.fact: The James River Bridge has a central roadway span that lifts straight up between towers so tall ships can pass beneath it.
cards.lengthNote: VDOT describes the current crossing as 4.5 miles; bridge-only inventory measurements are about 4.4 miles.
cards.openedNote: Current four-lane lift bridge completed in 1982; the original bridge opened in 1928.
cards.imageCredit: Tony Alter from Newport News, USA · CC BY 2.0
cards.originalFilename: Lift span of James River Bridge at sunset (2011).jpg

cards.name: San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge
cards.fact: The Bay Bridge links San Francisco and Oakland through Yerba Buena Island. Its eastern span was replaced in 2013.
cards.lengthNote: Crossing via Yerba Buena Island: 4.46 miles, excluding land approaches.
cards.openedNote: Original crossing opened in 1936; the eastern span was replaced in 2013.

cards.name: Tacoma Narrows Bridge
cards.fact: Two suspension bridges cross the Tacoma Narrows. The first of today’s pair opened in 1950 after the original 1940 bridge collapsed.
cards.lengthNote: One bridge: 5,400 ft; the two parallel bridges are not added together.
cards.openedNote: First surviving span opened in 1950; its twin opened in 2007. The original 1940 bridge collapsed.

cards.name: Lake Pontchartrain Causeway
cards.fact: The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway stretches almost 24 miles across a lake in Louisiana, with thousands of short spans supporting the road.
cards.lengthNote: Longer parallel span: 23.87 miles. The two bridges are not added together.
cards.openedNote: First span opened in 1956; the longer parallel span opened in 1969.
cards.imageCredit: formulanone from Huntsville, United States · CC BY-SA 2.0

cards.name: New River Gorge Bridge
cards.fact: The New River Gorge Bridge carries a roadway high above a deep West Virginia gorge on a huge steel arch.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: 3,030 ft; the arch span alone is 1,700 ft.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1977; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Royal Gorge Bridge
cards.fact: The Royal Gorge Bridge hangs high above Colorado’s Arkansas River, giving visitors a view down into the rocky gorge.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: 1,260 ft; height above the river is a different measurement.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1929; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Seven Mile Bridge

location.label: Marathon–Little Duck Key, Florida, United States

cards.fact: The Seven Mile Bridge carries the Overseas Highway through the Florida Keys. The modern road bridge runs beside parts of the older railway bridge.
cards.lengthNote: Modern bridge length: about 6.765 miles, despite its rounded name.
cards.openedNote: Modern road bridge opened in 1982; the separate original railway bridge opened in 1912.

cards.name: Mike O’Callaghan–Pat Tillman Memorial Bridge
cards.fact: This concrete arch bridge crosses the Colorado River beside Hoover Dam, carrying highway traffic between Nevada and Arizona.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: 1,900 ft; excludes the longer bypass highway project.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2010; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.imageCredit: Mariordo (Mario Roberto Durán Ortiz) · CC BY-SA 4.0

cards.name: Astoria–Megler Bridge
cards.fact: The Astoria–Megler Bridge crosses the mouth of the Columbia River between Oregon and Washington, with a tall steel truss above the shipping channel.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: 21,474 ft; the tall truss is only part of the crossing.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1966; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Eads Bridge

location.label: St. Louis, Missouri–East St. Louis, Illinois, United States

cards.fact: The Eads Bridge crosses the Mississippi River at St. Louis on three steel arches, carrying a road above railway tracks.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge and approaches: 6,442 ft; the central arch spans 520 ft.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1874; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Arthur Ravenel Jr. Bridge

location.label: Charleston–Mount Pleasant, South Carolina, United States

cards.fact: The Arthur Ravenel Jr. Bridge crosses the Cooper River in South Carolina. Its diamond-shaped towers hold the road with slanting cables.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge and approaches: 13,200 ft; the central span is 1,546 ft.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2005; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.originalFilename: Ravenel Bridge at night from Mt Pleasant.jpg

cards.name: Leonard P. Zakim Bunker Hill Memorial Bridge
cards.fact: Boston’s Zakim Bridge crosses the Charles River with two tall towers and fans of cables. Its name honors civil-rights leader Leonard Zakim and Bunker Hill.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: 1,432 ft; the main span is 745 ft.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2003; the year refers to the named structure.
cards.originalFilename: Zakim Bridge and railroad bridge Boston P1010835.jpg

cards.name: Holland Tunnel

location.label: Manhattan, New York–Jersey City, New Jersey, United States

cards.fact: The Holland Tunnel carries vehicles beneath the Hudson River. A powerful ventilation system moves fresh air through its two tubes.
cards.lengthNote: Longer westbound tube: 8,558 ft; eastbound tube is 8,371 ft. Parallel tubes are not added together.
cards.openedNote: Both original road tubes opened in 1927.

cards.name: Lincoln Tunnel

location.label: Manhattan, New York–Weehawken, New Jersey, United States

cards.fact: The Lincoln Tunnel links Midtown Manhattan and New Jersey beneath the Hudson River. Its three traffic tubes opened in different years.
cards.lengthNote: Longest (center) tube: 8,216 ft; the three tubes have different lengths.
cards.openedNote: First (center) tube opened in 1937; the north and south tubes followed in 1945 and 1957.

cards.name: Eisenhower–Johnson Memorial Tunnel
cards.fact: The Eisenhower–Johnson tunnels carry I-70 through the Rocky Mountains beneath the Continental Divide, high above sea level.
cards.lengthNote: Longer Johnson bore: 1.697 miles, rounded to 1.70; Eisenhower bore is 1.693 miles.
cards.openedNote: Eisenhower bore opened in 1973; Johnson bore opened in 1979.

cards.name: Fort McHenry Tunnel
cards.fact: The Fort McHenry Tunnel carries I-95 beneath Baltimore’s harbor in four tubes, with two traffic lanes in each tube.
cards.lengthNote: MDTA describes the tunnel as nearly 1.4 miles; excludes the full I-95 approach project.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1985; the year refers to the named structure.

cards.name: Anton Anderson Memorial Tunnel
cards.fact: Cars and trains take turns using the same narrow tunnel to Whittier, Alaska. It began as a railway tunnel and opened to road traffic in 2000.
cards.lengthNote: DOT visitor reference: about 2.5 miles through Maynard Mountain; not the 11.59-mile access highway.
cards.openedNote: Railway tunnel opened in 1943; shared road-and-rail operation began in 2000.

cards.name: Chesapeake Bay Bridge
cards.fact: The Chesapeake Bay Bridge links Maryland’s western and eastern shores. Unlike Virginia’s Chesapeake Bay Bridge–Tunnel, this crossing stays above the water.
cards.lengthNote: Longer eastbound span: 21,273 ft; the two parallel bridges are not added together.
cards.openedNote: First span opened in 1952; the parallel span opened in 1973.
cards.originalFilename: Chesapeake Bay Bridge from Annapolis to Maryland's Eastern Shore LCCN2011632486-2.jpg

cards.name: Pont du Gard
cards.fact: The Romans built Pont du Gard with three levels of stone arches to carry water across the Gardon River toward Nîmes.
cards.lengthNote: Length of the surviving upper tier: 275 m. The lower tiers are shorter; the full Nîmes aqueduct ran for about 50 km.
cards.openedNote: Built around 50 CE, within an estimated 40–60 CE construction period. This is an approximate ancient construction date, not a recorded opening year.
cards.imageAlt: Pont du Gard with three tiers of stone arches above the Gardon River

cards.name: Stari Most

location.label: Neretva River, Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina

cards.fact: Stari Most curves over the Neretva River in one steep stone arch. Its name means Old Bridge, and it was rebuilt to match the original 1566 bridge.
cards.lengthNote: Approx. 30 m for the whole stone bridge; the arch opening is about 27 m.
cards.openedNote: The reconstructed bridge reopened in 2004. The original opened in 1566 and was destroyed in 1993.
cards.imageAlt: The reconstructed Stari Most stone arch between two towers over the Neretva River

cards.name: Clifton Suspension Bridge

location.label: Avon Gorge, Bristol, England, United Kingdom

cards.fact: Clifton Suspension Bridge hangs above Bristol’s Avon Gorge from iron chains. Isambard Kingdom Brunel began its design when he was only 24.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: 412 m; the suspended main span between the towers is about 214 m.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1864, after Brunel’s death; engineers John Hawkshaw and William Henry Barlow completed the design.
cards.imageAlt: Clifton Suspension Bridge spanning the Avon Gorge between its stone towers

cards.name: Széchenyi Chain Bridge
cards.fact: The Széchenyi Chain Bridge was the first permanent bridge joining Buda and Pest across the Danube. Heavy iron chains support its roadway.
cards.lengthNote: Approx. 380 m across all three spans; the central span is about 203 m. Some references round the overall length differently.
cards.openedNote: First opened in 1849. The bridge was rebuilt after wartime destruction and reopened in 1949.
cards.imageAlt: The illuminated Széchenyi Chain Bridge crossing the Danube at night
cards.originalFilename: Széchenyi Chain Bridge in Budapest at night.jpg

cards.name: Chapel Bridge
cards.fact: Lucerne’s Chapel Bridge has a wooden roof with triangular paintings beneath it. The covered walkway passes beside an octagonal water tower.
cards.lengthNote: Present bridge length: about 204.7 m; the medieval bridge was longer before later shoreline changes.
cards.openedNote: Originally built around 1365. Much of the wooden structure was rebuilt after a 1993 fire and reopened in 1994.
cards.imageAlt: Lucerne’s wooden Chapel Bridge beside its octagonal stone water tower

cards.name: The Iron Bridge

location.label: River Severn, Ironbridge, England, United Kingdom

cards.fact: The Iron Bridge showed that cast iron could support a large bridge. Its curved ribs were assembled from separate iron pieces made in local furnaces.
cards.lengthNote: Approx. 60 m overall including the approach spans; the main cast-iron arch spans 30.63 m.
cards.openedNote: Formally opened to traffic in 1781. The main iron arch had been erected in 1779.
cards.imageAlt: The red cast-iron arch and circular ironwork of the Iron Bridge over the River Severn
cards.originalFilename: Iron Bridge east side in February 2019 (cropped).jpg

cards.name: Glenfinnan Viaduct
cards.fact: Glenfinnan Viaduct curves through the Scottish Highlands on 21 concrete arches. It appears in the Harry Potter films carrying the Hogwarts Express.
cards.lengthNote: Total curved railway viaduct length: about 381 m (1,250 ft), across 21 arches.
cards.openedNote: Opened for regular railway service in 1901; construction of the viaduct itself was completed in 1898.
cards.imageAlt: The tall concrete arches of Glenfinnan Viaduct in the Scottish Highlands

cards.name: Bridge of Sighs
cards.fact: Venice’s Bridge of Sighs is an enclosed stone passage over a canal. It connected the Doge’s Palace to the prison on the opposite bank.
cards.lengthNote: Whole bridge: about 11 m, rounded to 0.01 mi for gameplay. It is a short enclosed canal crossing.
cards.openedNote: Built around 1600, in the early 1600s. The game uses an approximate construction year rather than a documented opening date.
cards.imageAlt: The enclosed white limestone Bridge of Sighs above a narrow Venetian canal

cards.name: Puente Nuevo
cards.fact: Puente Nuevo joins the two sides of Ronda above a deep gorge. A chamber inside the bridge’s tall central arch once served as a prison.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: about 66 m across the gorge. The roughly 98 m height is a different measurement.
cards.openedNote: Opened to horses and carriages in 1787, according to Ronda’s tourism office. Construction, including the aqueduct work, finished in 1793.
cards.imageAlt: Puente Nuevo’s tall stone piers and arches rising from the gorge at Ronda

cards.name: 25 de Abril Bridge
cards.fact: Lisbon’s red 25 de Abril Bridge carries cars on its upper deck and trains below. The railway deck opened more than 30 years after the road.
cards.lengthNote: Approx. 2.3 km for the suspension bridge itself, excluding the northern approach viaduct and access roads; the main span is about 1,013 m.
cards.openedNote: The road bridge opened in 1966; the lower railway deck opened in 1999.
cards.imageAlt: The red towers and cables of Lisbon’s 25 de Abril Bridge above the Tagus River

cards.name: Vasco da Gama Bridge
cards.fact: The Vasco da Gama Bridge stretches across Lisbon’s broad Tagus estuary. Its long rows of piers lead to a taller section held up by diagonal cables.
cards.lengthNote: Full crossing including viaducts and approach sections: about 17.2 km. The cable-stayed main bridge is only one part of this route.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1998; the year refers to the completed Tagus crossing.
cards.imageAlt: Vasco da Gama Bridge’s cable-stayed section and long line of piers across the Tagus estuary
cards.originalFilename: Vasco da Gama Bridge aerial view.jpg

cards.name: 1915 Çanakkale Bridge
cards.fact: The 1915 Çanakkale Bridge links Europe and Asia across the Dardanelles. Its 2,023-meter central span was the world’s longest suspension span when it opened.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge with approach viaducts: 4,608 m; the unsupported central suspension span is 2,023 m.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2022. The 1915 in the bridge’s name commemorates a historical event, not its opening year.
cards.imageAlt: The red-and-white towers and suspension cables of the 1915 Çanakkale Bridge

cards.name: Helix Bridge
cards.fact: Singapore’s Helix Bridge curls around its walkway like the double spiral of DNA. Its two twisting steel structures work together to hold the bridge up.
cards.lengthNote: Total pedestrian bridge length: 280 m. This is the curved Helix walkway, not the adjacent road bridge.
cards.openedNote: First opened in April 2010; the remaining section opened in July of the same year.
cards.imageAlt: The illuminated double-spiral steel frame of Singapore’s Helix Bridge

cards.name: Langkawi Sky Bridge
cards.fact: Langkawi Sky Bridge curves high above a forested valley, held by cables from a single leaning tower. Builders used helicopters to lift parts onto the mountain.
cards.lengthNote: Length of the curved pedestrian bridge: 125 m. The cable car and SkyGlide lift are separate structures.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2005; it reopened in 2015 following maintenance and upgrades.
cards.imageCredit: Flickr user "The Dilly Lama" · CC BY 2.0
cards.imageAlt: The curved Langkawi Sky Bridge suspended from one tower above a forested valley

cards.name: Golden Bridge

location.label: Bà Nà Hills, near Da Nang, Vietnam

cards.fact: Vietnam’s Golden Bridge looks as if two giant stone hands are lifting its golden walkway. The hands are modern sculptures made to look ancient.
cards.lengthNote: Length of the pedestrian bridge: 150 m; the height of the mountain resort is not the bridge’s length.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 2018 at the Bà Nà Hills resort.
cards.imageAlt: Two enormous sculpted hands appearing to support the Golden Bridge in Vietnam
cards.originalFilename: Golden Bridge at Ba Na Hills 20250718.jpg

cards.name: Howrah Bridge
cards.fact: Howrah Bridge joins Kolkata and Howrah with a giant steel framework. Its cantilever arms reach out from the banks, leaving the river’s main channel free of piers.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: about 705 m; the central span is about 457 m.
cards.openedNote: The current cantilever bridge opened in 1943, replacing an earlier floating pontoon bridge.
cards.imageAlt: Howrah Bridge’s illuminated steel cantilever framework over the Hooghly River

cards.name: Victoria Falls Bridge

location.label: Zambezi River below Victoria Falls, Zambia–Zimbabwe border

cards.fact: Victoria Falls Bridge crosses the Zambezi gorge just downstream from the waterfall. Its steel arch links Zambia and Zimbabwe where spray can drift over passing trains.
cards.lengthNote: Total bridge length: about 198 m (650 ft); the main steel arch spans about 152 m.
cards.openedNote: Opened in 1905; the date refers to the original steel bridge.
cards.imageAlt: Victoria Falls Bridge’s steel arch high above the Zambezi gorge
cards.originalFilename: Puente de las cataratas Victoria, Zambia-Zimbabue, 2018-07-27, DD 10.jpg

cards.name: Confederation Bridge

location.label: Northumberland Strait, Prince Edward Island–New Brunswick, Canada

cards.fact: Confederation Bridge links Prince Edward Island to mainland Canada across water that freezes in winter. Its curved route replaced a ferry crossing.
cards.lengthNote: Full bridge length: 12.9 km, including the approach sections across Northumberland Strait.
cards.openedNote: Opened to traffic in 1997.
cards.imageAlt: The long curved Confederation Bridge crossing Northumberland Strait
cards.originalFilename: Confederation Bridge aerial view (from PEI side).jpg

cards.name: Mont Blanc Tunnel
cards.fact: Mont Blanc Tunnel takes drivers beneath the Alps between France and Italy. For much of the trip, more than two kilometers of rock lie overhead.
cards.lengthNote: One road tunnel, about 11.6 km long. This is the full bore between the French and Italian portals.
cards.openedNote: Opened to traffic in 1965. It reopened in 2002 after the 1999 fire and extensive reconstruction.
cards.imageCredit: Photo prise par François Trazzi · CC BY-SA 3.0
cards.imageAlt: The Italian entrance of Mont Blanc Tunnel beneath a white arch

cards.name: Marmaray Bosphorus Tunnel

location.label: Bosphorus seabed between Sirkeci and Üsküdar, Istanbul, Turkey

cards.fact: Marmaray trains travel between Europe and Asia beneath the Bosphorus. Engineers lowered giant tunnel sections into a trench in the seabed and joined them underwater.
cards.lengthNote: Immersed undersea section only: 1,387 m. Excludes the land tunnels, the 13.6 km initial crossing project, and the longer Marmaray railway.
cards.openedNote: Opened for passenger services in 2013; the wider Marmaray railway was expanded in 2019.
cards.imageAlt: Railway tracks inside the Marmaray tunnel beneath the Bosphorus

cards.name: Atal Tunnel
cards.fact: Atal Tunnel runs beneath Rohtang Pass in the Himalayas. It gives the Lahaul valley a road connection even when deep snow blocks the mountain pass.
cards.lengthNote: Full road tunnel length: 9.02 km; the emergency passage is within the same structure and is not added to the length.
cards.openedNote: Inaugurated in October 2020.
cards.imageAlt: A car traveling through the broad, illuminated interior of Atal Tunnel

cards.name: Guoliang Tunnel

location.label: Taihang Mountains, Guoliang village, Henan, China

cards.fact: Villagers carved Guoliang Tunnel through a cliff to give their village a road to the outside world. Openings in the rock act like windows along the route.
cards.lengthNote: Approx. 1.25 km for the cliff tunnel road; some sources round this to 1.2 km.
cards.openedNote: Opened to traffic in 1977 after work began in 1972.
cards.imageCredit: FANG Chen from Beijing, China · CC BY 2.0
cards.imageAlt: The row of openings along Guoliang Tunnel cut into a sheer cliff

cards.name: SMART Tunnel

location.label: SMART Tunnel near the Bukit Bintang junction, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia

cards.fact: Kuala Lumpur’s SMART Tunnel carries traffic and diverts floodwater. During severe storms, cars leave and the road section can fill with water to help protect the city.
cards.lengthNote: Full stormwater bypass tunnel: 9.7 km. Only part also carries cars; the motorway route is about 4 km including its entrance and exit sections.
cards.openedNote: The motorway and stormwater system opened in stages in 2007.
cards.imageAlt: Cars inside one of the road levels of Kuala Lumpur’s SMART Tunnel

cards.name: Thames Tunnel

location.label: River Thames, Rotherhithe–Wapping, London, United Kingdom

cards.fact: The Thames Tunnel was the first tunnel built successfully beneath a river used by ships. It opened for pedestrians before being converted to carry trains.
cards.lengthNote: Approx. 396 m (1,300 ft) for the historic river tunnel, excluding its vertical entrance shafts; the parallel passages are not added together.
cards.openedNote: Opened for pedestrians in 1843; railway services began in 1869.
cards.imageCredit: Lars Plougmann from United States · CC BY-SA 2.0
cards.imageAlt: The arched interior and railway tracks of the historic Thames Tunnel

cards.name: Simplon Tunnel
cards.fact: Simplon Tunnel carries trains beneath the Alps between Switzerland and Italy. It was the world’s longest railway tunnel when its first bore opened in 1906.
cards.lengthNote: First (eastern) bore: 19.803 km. The parallel western bore is 19.823 km long and is not added to this figure.
cards.openedNote: The first bore opened in 1906; the second opened in 1921.
cards.imageAlt: The two southern railway portals of Simplon Tunnel near Iselle, Italy
